Hi Jordan / Priya  thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of what I heard:
- Primary requirement: private connectivity due to regulated PII workflow (HIPAA-adjacent).
- Traffic profile: baseline low-to-moderate, expect spikes during business hours (we'll need to confirm QPS later).
- Preference: Private VPC or Dedicated with private connectivity; Hosted API is acceptable only if we can guarantee network controls.

Redwood deployment options (high level):
- Hosted API: fastest to start, no network changes required, but less control over IP allowlists/private peering.
- Dedicated capacity: Reserved GPUs for predictable throughput + optional IP allowlists / peering.
- Private VPC (recommended for strict isolation): deploys with customer VPC peering or PrivateLink, supports KMS/HSM and audit logs.

Hi Jordan / Priya  Marissa from Solutions / SRE here. Great to meet you on the thread  below are the practical networking options and the minimal checklist we use for Private VPC setups.

Connectivity options we support:
- AWS PrivateLink (recommended for minimal routing changes): we expose a PrivateLink endpoint in your account; requires VPC endpoint service acceptance and SG rules from your side.
- VPC Peering (supported): simpler for same-region setups, but routing is managed by your team; peering is typically used for Dedicated/Private on-prem setups.

Minimal network checklist (what we typically need from your side):
- VPC CIDR(s) for the subnets that will talk to Redwood (example: 10.0.0.0/16).
- Public/private subnets where PrivateLink endpoints will be created (for PrivateLink) or peering subnets for peering.
- Security group rules: allow outbound HTTPS (443) to Redwood egress IPs (we'll provide list), and allow inbound from our PrivateLink ENIs if applicable.
- NAT/Egress: if you require egress IP allowlisting on your side, let us know and we will provide our egress ranges. Note: for PrivateLink, traffic stays in AWS and egress IPs are generally not required.
- TLS/certs: we support customer-managed certificates (ACM) for mutual TLS if needed; otherwise standard TLS is fine.
- KMS: we can integrate with customer-managed KMS for encryption-at-rest in Private deployments.

Ports & protocols (minimal):
- TCP 443 (HTTPS) outbound from your app-hosts to Redwood endpoints
- For health checks/metrics we may need TCP 443 inbound to our monitoring endpoints if you opt into managed monitoring (optional).

Attachments: I've uploaded a one-page network checklist and an example security group rule set (network-checklist.xlsx).

Next steps:
- Jordan: please share your VPC CIDR and a simple network diagram before the call.
- We propose Wed 14 Jul 10:00am PT for a 30m SRE call  Sean, can you confirm?

If helpful, Rishi (cc) can join to discuss Dedicated capacity sizing if you want reserved throughput rather than multi-tenant capacity.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
